text:
Alex: Thinking out loud — proposal for a hybrid pool handoff that keeps a small stable on-demand floor and uses short-lived spot burst pools for spikes. Goal: keep 99th latency SLO and cut spot cost w/o risky mass preemptions.

Priya: +1 to exploring. what min on-demand floor are you thinking?

Alex: Start conservative: 12% of steady-state GPU count per region as guaranteed on-demand. Floor tessellated per-AZ rather than global to avoid cross-AZ egress during failovers.

Martin: curious how you picked 12%. is that based on p95 load or a safety multiplier?

Alex: p95 steady-concurrency * 1.15 safety buffer, tuned per-service. For small fleets that rounds to that ~10-15% range. We can make it a configurable percentile: floor_percent = max(5, percentile(95)*1.15).

Lina: interruption handling for the burst pools? we need KV-cache warmup and request draining strategy so inference latency doesn’t spike.

Alex: plan: short-lived spot instances are added to a burst pool with two-phase handoff: (1) soft-add: pre-warm model + KV cache by replaying recent prefixes for pinned customers, (2) promote: mark as available for new requests. on preemption signal, we soft-drain new arrivals and redirect to on-demand floor or other AZ.

Sasha: how do we detect preemption early enough? cloud preempt notifications often give seconds.

Alex: rely on provider interruption webhook + a short-lived heartbeat between runtime and orchestrator. On webhook, orchestrator marks node draining and signals the serving runtime to publish remaining token cache to a fast remote cache (s3/redis) for fast rebuild on fallback. also re-route ephemeral sessions to a hot standby.

Priya: re: cache publish — that adds egress and storage ops. cost tradeoff? sometimes repopulating from disk is cheaper than publishing KV for many small sessions.

Alex: agreed. heuristic: only publish KV if live session length > 128 tokens OR if user is high-SLA. default fallback is rebuild from model checkpoints and incremental replay. We can expose policy per-customer.

Martin: any changes needed in autoscaler? current scales by GPU utilization and queue depth. burst pools need proactive scaling based on ingress prediction so they pre-warm ahead of spikes.

Alex: yes — add prediction-driven warm-up: short-window rate forecasting (30s-2m) using recent request rates + A/B short experiments. If predicted spike, spin up burst nodes into soft-add state.

Lina: region constraints: some regions have tiny spot pools. If we attempt aggressive burst there we risk capacity exhaustion. Do we have fallback policies?

Alex: fallback hierarchy: same-AZ on-demand floor -> same-region other AZ -> cross-region burst (only if latency budget allows) -> queue with degraded QoS. Also limit cross-region to non-PII customers.

Sasha: can we express the policy in a simple config? e.g.:

```
policy:
  min_on_demand_percent: 12
  burst_warmup_secs: 45
  publish_kv_if_tokens_gt: 128
  fallback_order: [az_on_demand, region_az, cross_region, degrade]
  cross_region_allowed_for: [non_pii]
```

Alex: exactly. keep defaults safe, allow per-customer override.

Priya: testing approach? we need a chaos test for spot churn + network partitions that attempts to validate no more than X% request error increase.

Martin: propose canary: 5% traffic run through the new handoff, synthetic spike generator, and controlled preempt events (simulate webhook). measure 99th lat and error delta.

Lina: also add KV-rebuild time metric and egress cost per publish event to the observability dashboard.

Sasha: ops question: who owns the rollout? infra core for autoscaler + runtime team for soft-add/drain + platform for per-customer policy UI.

Alex: yep. will draft RFC with config schema, autoscaler changes, runtime hooks, and a short test plan. target PRD by next Wed. comments welcome. :pray:

capacity-bot: [capacity snapshot] region-us-west1: on-demand=120 GPUs, spot-burst=40 GPUs (available), predicted spike +18% in 90s

Priya: thanks — please tag me on the RFC, I'll add chaos tests.

Martin: +1, and add a cost-sim scenario so finance can see projected savings vs risk.

Lina: also include a sample rollback: instant disable of spot-burst via feature flag + enforced floor.

Alex: will do. finishing notes: keep the floor per-customer configurable, autoscaler should allow both reactive and predictive modes, and eviction policy should favor non-critical sessions.

Sasha: sounds good. low-risk rollout plan. :thumbsup:
